I propose one vertical ticket, based on revision 1 of work/offline-note-title-search/spec.md:

1. **Title:** Deliver offline note title search CLI
   **Blocked by:** None (explicitly empty blockers).
   **What it delivers:** A runnable, documented command that reads a supplied UTF-8 JSON notes file, validates it, searches titles case-insensitively, and prints matches in input order. Include external command tests through the approved temporary-file seam.

   **Observable acceptance criteria:**
   - A documented invocation accepts a file path and query, including an empty query.
   - Literal substring queries match titles case-insensitively; printed titles retain their original spelling, order, and duplicates.
   - Body-only matches are excluded. No matches and an empty list produce empty stdout and exit zero.
   - An empty query prints every title in order; UTF-8 text is preserved.
   - Malformed JSON, a non-list root, non-object entries, missing title/body fields, or non-string field values produce a diagnostic and nonzero exit, with no partial title output.
   - Invalid UTF-8 and unreadable files produce diagnostics and nonzero exit.
   - The command works offline and creates no persistent application storage.
   - Automated tests invoke the command with temporary input files and inspect stdout and exit status, plus stderr for error diagnostics. Delivery includes instructions to run the command and tests.

This small feature fits one independently verifiable slice; splitting parsing, search, and tests would fragment the same user behavior. No prefactoring is needed in this new repository.

Does this single-ticket granularity feel right, are the empty blocking edges correct, and would you prefer any split? I have not published a ticket. The [to-tickets skill](C:/Users/vince/.codex/skills/to-tickets/SKILL.md) says, “Iterate until the user approves the breakdown,” and you explicitly requested approval before publication.
